function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times. Early observations were made by Thales of Miletus (around 600 BCE) who noted that rubbing amber produced static attraction. In the 17th century, William Gilbert coined the term *electricus* and studied electrical phenomena. Later, Benjamin Franklin’s kite experiment (1752) helped establish the nature of lightning as electricity. Subsequent scientists such as Alessandro Volta, Michael Faraday, and James Clerk Maxwell built on these foundations to develop the modern science of electromagnetism.
